graph.name: Payson Drilling Data Mart Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture illustrating Payson's unified drilling data mart platform leveraging Presto on EMR, Hive ETL workflows, RDS MySQL metadata storage, and EMRFS for queryable sensor data in S3.

nodes.name: DATAMART USER
nodes.notes: Contractors and operators responsible for drilling oil and gas wells, accessing Presto via JDBC/ODBC drivers.

nodes.name: PRESTO
nodes.notes: Apache Presto interface running on EMR providing a unified query view across sensor data and metadata.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Compute instances running microservices including authentication plugins and the Datamart ETL orchestration service.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores high-volume raw sensor data (500 channels at 1-second frequency across over 700,000 wells).

nodes.name: HIVE
nodes.notes: Data processing component commanded by ETL microservices to create tables around raw S3 files and perform transformations.

nodes.name: EMR FS
nodes.notes: Consistent S3 view layer storing high-volume sensor data loaded by Hive for querying via Presto.

nodes.name: RDS MYSQL
nodes.notes: MySQL database storing frequently changing well metadata across 700,000 database instances in a star schema.

nodes.name: EMR HDFS
nodes.notes: Hadoop Distributed File System component within the EMR cluster environment.

edges.notes: Datamart ETL microservice on EC2 accesses raw sensor files stored in S3.
EC2 orchestrator commands Hive to transform data and create a Hive table around S3 files.
Hive loads transformed sensor data into EMRFS.
Datamart users query the unified dataset via Presto using JDBC/ODBC.
Presto invokes custom authentication and authorization microservices running on EC2.
Presto queries high-volume sensor data residing in EMRFS.
Presto queries frequently changing well metadata stored in RDS MySQL.
